title: Read project intent back after .tenet/ is lost (CON-07)
body:
## What

PRD CON-07: "If `.tenet/` is lost, Tenet shall reconstruct from repository memory and Git history, ask only consequential unknowns and never fabricate evidence."

At the first `open` with **no state document**, if the repository has Tenet's marks (managed blocks in `INTENT.md`, damaged markers, `Tenet-Work` trailers, or unmerged `tenet/` branches):

- A `reconstructed-from-repository` note (new reason code, exit 0) lists which shared files are present, commits per work label in Git history (all refs), unmerged `tenet/` branches, shallow history, blocks it could not read, and a fixed list of what **cannot** be recovered (grants, consents, approvals, receipts, review judgments, locks, adoption/trust, contracts and budgets, verification and test links, plan-item links and states, decision quotes).
- The work label sequence continues past the highest label in history (e.g. `W-0007` in history means the new contract is `W-0008`), whatever the answer.
- If `INTENT.md` has blocks that read back exactly, one chat question, `reconstruction-review` (exit 3), is bound to the hash of the recovered content. Other calls are fenced until it is answered, the same way quarantine is. `decide adopt --target reconstruction --answer reconstruction-review=use` loads the recovered content as **unadopted** intent and records `project.reconstructed` (IDs and what was not recovered). `=fresh` keeps an empty intent. If `INTENT.md` changed after the question, nothing is recovered and the question is asked again.
- `INTENT.md` and Git are only read.

Never fabricated: no grant, consent, receipt, trust entry, lock, review or contract is created. `adoption.intent` stays `undecided`. Recovered elements have `origin: "tenet"` and `verifiedBy: []`, plan items come back `proposed` with no element links, and decision records have no quote. A block is recovered only when re-rendering what was read gives the file's text again (new pure `core/reconstruct.ts`, the inverse of `renderIntent`); any other block is listed as not recovered.

## Simplifications (disclosed; not a full implementation of TS §15.3 / UX §6 / local `specs/reconstruction.md`)

- No `docs/decisions/` or test-tag scan, no proposed lock manifest, and no policy or charter re-adoption flow beyond saying the files must be adopted again.
- No 500-commit bound: the trailer scan reads all refs.
- Damaged markers do **not** stop `open` (TS §7.8 says stop). They produce an `intent-markers-invalid` note and nothing is recovered.
- It does not ask which unfinished work to resume. Unmerged `tenet/` branches are listed as facts; their contracts are lost.
- Offered only at the first `open` with no state document. After a quarantine both questions are queued, quarantine first; that ordering is **not tested**.
- `inspect` does not mention reconstruction.
- ID allocators are not seeded after a decline, so a new ID may equal one in `INTENT.md` (that block is then kept as a human edit).
- `project.reconstructed` is a new optional field in a non-strict object, so an older kernel drops it on write.
- Prior adoption is unknown: the same repository content after an adopted or a declined history is treated the same.
- No independent review or owner sign-off of the contract. The spec's §14 gaps remain open.

## Tests (`packages/kernel/test/reconstruction.test.ts`, all tagged `[CON-07]`)

- Parser round trip of every block kind; a hand-edited block is skipped; damaged markers recover nothing. Runs on every platform.
- `GitCli.tenetHistory` on real Git: labels per commit on all refs, a forged `W-99999999999` ignored, unmerged versus merged `tenet/` branches. Runs on every platform.
- Five `open` tests (POSIX only, since the kernel refuses mutating work on Windows): one question, label `W-0008`, no authority or evidence, fence, accept, asked once; decline; stale answer; a real adopt → `rm -r .tenet` → reconstruct; no marks means no change.

## Interaction with GIT-09

`shared-merge.test.ts` commits managed `INTENT.md` blocks before its first `open`. With no `.tenet/`, that is the CON-07 footprint, so `open` now asks `reconstruction-review`, which blocks `finish` until answered. The test setup now asserts the question and answers `fresh`; the GIT-09 behavior under test is unchanged.

## Local checks (Windows)

- Typecheck, `lint-arch`, `lint-skills` and `lint-quality` pass.
- `npm run privacy` and the privacy range check pass.
- `coverage --milestone R1`: CON-07 is now mapped. It still exits 1 because of other unmapped Musts (EVD-04, QLT-05), several of which other sessions are building.
- The five `open` tests have **not run locally**; they run only in this PR's Linux and macOS CI.
